summary: Async production host now decides prompt mode/expected_turn_id at admission against its active-jobs map: start_if_idle while a prompt/steer job (or deferred steer) exists for the project is refused immediately with retryable not_idle; an expected_turn_id that differs from the active job's published turn ID is refused immediately with expected_turn_mismatch; a prompt with mode=steer (no attachments) while a turn runs takes the same cancel-and-reissue PendingSteer path as the steer command (responses echo command 'prompt'). Idle cases still defer to Agent::submit.
commands_run: cargo test --locked --test headless_protocol --test headless_domain_owner --test headless_event_budget --test headless_input_shutdown --test headless_project_workspace

validation_result.validator_run_async_streams_start_if_idl: pass: async_start_if_idle_is_rejected_at_admission_while_a_slow_prompt_runs (fails on origin/main: response never arrives while the slow prompt is held open)
validation_result.remote_headless_commands: pass; production_plain_host_routes_authenticated_tls_prompt_to_the_provider failed once under parallel load, passed rerun with --test-threads=1

notes: No new unwrap/expect/panic in non-test code, no unsafe, no new Arc<Mutex>. Default mode start_or_steer while busy is unchanged (still queues), because many clients rely on back-to-back prompts queueing; only explicit mode=steer is routed to the steer path. Note: Cargo has no 'remote' feature; remote tests run in the default build.
